messages:
Alex: Heads up — seeing a subtle nvme latency fingerprint in eu-central that correlates with GPU provisioning failures for small batch jobs. Provisioning queues stalled ~50s on average. Logs below.

alert-bot: [ALERT] nvme_iops_spike node=gpu-node-117 eu-central-1 2026-03-18T10:12:03Z

Jamie: Ugh, we hit that pattern last month. Any correlation with scrub window or janitor runs?

Alex: Yes — 10/10 correlation with ephemeral-scrub cron at 10:10. When scrub overlaps with spike, scratchpool thrash + eviction starve.

Rohan: Can you paste iostat/blkstat? Also which firmware on those NVMe devices?

Alex: snippet:
```
iostat -x 1 3
Device:         r/s    w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  avgqu-sz await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1        8.2   420.1  67104  345600  12.7  63.2   1.45  98.3
nvme1n1        0.1   12.5   128   1024   0.4   1.2    0.30   3.7
```
fw: PM2048_v3.2.1

Sasha: %util 98 on nvme0n1 — that's brutal. Are these nodes running large batch prefetch jobs or heavy KV cache writes?

Alex: Mostly caching + prefix writes from model loads. Also observed overlapping janitor deletes. I think small-block churn is spinning up GC paths.

Jamie: Two immediate mitigations:
1) push scrub window by 30m in eu-central
2) reduce janitor concurrency from 64 -> 16 for scratchpool

Rohan: Can we route new gpu allocations away from affected nodes until we patch? Maybe mark with node label `scratch_throttle=true`.

Alex: I can run a quick taint: `kubectl taint nodes gpu-node-1 scratch_throttle=true:NoSchedule` for 50 hosts.

Sasha: Long-term: need to evaluate firmware rollback or NVMe vendor patch. Also consider moving heavy model cache to dedicated capacity or ephemeral cache tier on remote SSDs.

Alex: Cost concern: moving to networked SSDs will increase egress + latency and add ~$0.08/token equivalent for our benchmark — ops wants to avoid unless necessary.

Jamie: Plan agreed: implement mitigations now, schedule firmware trial on 10 nodes for canary, and add a throttling knob to janitor. I'll open a PR for scrub-schedule change and janitor flag.

Rohan: I'll add an autoscaler hook to avoid scheduling GPU pods on nodes with iops_util>85%.

Alex: Thanks — will run the taint now and post followups. :thumbsup:

alert-bot: [RECOVERY] nvme_iops_spike cleared node=gpu-node-117 2026-03-18T10:45:31Z

Alex: After tainting, provisioning queue latency dropped to ~4s. Monitoring looks stable. Keeping scrub moved + janitor concurrency reduced.

Sasha: Good job. Let's sync in eng-infra tomorrow to confirm firmware canary and cost tradeoffs.
